title: Ethiopian Sautéed Beef
community: All of Ethiopia — the most universally ordered restaurant dish
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Beef Tibs — small cubes of beef sautéed fast and hot in kibbeh with onions, tomatoes, jalapeños, rosemary, and a touch of berbere until perfectly browned outside and juicy within. Ethiopia's most popular restaurant dish — fast, intensely flavoured, and utterly satisfying.
longDesc: Tibs is Ethiopia's restaurant staple — the dish ordered more than any other in Ethiopian restaurants worldwide. The technique is pure and fast: very hot kibbeh, beef cubes that sear quickly, onions, tomatoes, and the brightness of fresh jalapeño and rosemary. Done in 15 minutes, it is one of the fastest great dishes in African cooking.
ingredients: 600g beef sirloin or tenderloin — cut into 2cm cubes
equipment: Cast iron pan or heavy skillet
steps: Heat kibbeh in a heavy pan over high heat until smoking.
Add beef cubes in a single layer — do not crowd.
Sear without stirring for 2 minutes. Turn. Sear other sides.
Add onion. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Add garlic, jalapeño, and rosemary. Stir 1 minute.
Add berbere, black pepper, and salt.
Toss everything together for 1 more minute.
The beef should be medium-done — seared outside, still juicy within.
Serve immediately on injera or in the pan.
chefTips: Very hot pan is the most important step — if it doesn't sizzle aggressively when the beef goes in, the pan isn't hot enough.
Do not crowd — cook in batches if needed.
Tibs should take 12—15 minutes total — it's a fast dish.
Serve immediately — tibs waits for nobody.
Rosemary is the Ethiopian aromatic signature for tibs.
commonMistakes: Insufficiently hot pan — beef steams instead of sears.
cookingScience: The Maillard reaction on the beef cubes requires the surface temperature to reach 140°C — this is why the pan must be very hot before adding the beef. Any moisture on the beef surface must evaporate before browning can begin. Patting beef dry before cooking removes this moisture barrier.
servedWith: As part of an Ethiopian combination platter
culturalNote: Tibs is Ethiopia's everyday celebration — ordered when someone feels like something special without the full commitment of a wat. It is the most ordered dish at Ethiopian restaurants worldwide, loved by Ethiopians and international guests alike for its bold, immediate flavour.
